subject: Next steps: security artifacts, pen test report & vulnerability disclosure workflow
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Desai <pri@medalpha.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T15:02:00Z
Subject: Post-demo recap + security artifact asks

Hi Priyanka — thanks again for the demo today, great conversation. Quick recap and a few asks so we can move the security intake forward for your InfoSec and procurement teams:

- Redwood readiness: we support SOC 2 Type II and have HIPAA controls available on Private deployments.
- What we need from you: SOC 2 attestation (latest), any GDPR/HIPAA scoping notes, and the primary contact for receiving vulnerability reports.
- Vendor questionnaire: attaching a short vendor security questionnaire (redwood_vendor_questionnaire_v1.docx) — can you or your security team fill the highlighted sections and return?
- Pen test: several customers prefer we exchange a high-level pen test summary first and then sign an NDA/DocuSign to transfer the full report. If you have a 3rd-party pen test from the last 12 months, could you share the summary and let us know whether you can provide the full report under NDA?
- Vulnerability process: we typically propose a mutual disclosure SLA (we suggest 30 days for critical/high remediation, 60 days for medium, unless regulatory constraints require otherwise) and quarterly public scans plus annual external pentests. Does that align with MedAlpha policy?

Next steps I propose:
1) Priyanka: share SOC 2 and any pen-test summary by end of week (or point me to where we can pull it).
2) Redwood: Legal will send a DocuSign NDA if you can share the full PT report.
3) Both: align on vulnerability SLA and disclosure cadence — if OK, we’ll add it to the mutual action plan (link below).

Attachments: redwood_vendor_questionnaire_v1.docx (docx)
Mutual action plan (we'll add items): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-security

Thanks — I’ll loop Neha from Security once we have the SOC/pen-summary.

—Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Priyanka Desai <pri@medalpha.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: MedAlpha Security Team <security@medalpha.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + security artifact asks

Connor — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers from our side: 

- SOC 2: we have a SOC 2 Type II report for FY2025; I attached a one-page executive summary (MedAlpha-PT-2025-summary.pdf). The full attestation is under our vendor-sharing agreement but we can provide it via secure link after a quick NDA.
- HIPAA/GDPR: we operate under HIPAA; GDPR applies to our EU patient dataset (we host EU data in EU region). I'll attach our compliance summary in a separate note.
- Pen test: We had an external assessment in Nov 2025. I've attached the high-level findings summary; the full report is restricted and we can share under a signed NDA (we usually use DocuSign).
- Vulnerability SLA: our standard expectation is 45 days for critical/high vulnerabilities, 90 days for medium. We can be flexible depending on the severity and if production mitigation is required. We also run automated external scans monthly and full external pen tests annually.

Can you send over your NDA link and the vendor questionnaire backfilled with any Redwood-specific notes? Also please confirm if your disclosure SLA can be extended to 45 days for criticals — that's our preferred window.

Regards,
Priyanka Desai
Head of Security Operations | MedAlpha Inc
Attachments: MedAlpha-PT-2025-summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T12:45:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap + security artifact asks

Looping in Aditya and Neha — Priyanka shared the summary and wants an NDA for the full report. Can Legal/Contracts get DocuSign out today? Also we should confirm Redwood's standard disclosure SLA and whether we can accept 45 days for criticals for this deal (DEAL-9821).

Action items for Security/Legal: 
- Aditya: can you trigger the DocuSign NDA using the vendor-sharing template and include recipient pri@medalpha.com?
- Neha: please review the MedAlpha summary attached and confirm any red flags we should call out before full report transfer.

—Vanessa
VP, Commercial

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Desai <pri@medalpha.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T08:05:00Z
Subject: DocuSign: Redwood vendor-sharing NDA + questions on vulnerability SLA

Hi Priyanka — thanks for the summary. I've initiated a DocuSign envelope (link below) using our standard vendor-sharing NDA that covers transfer of sensitive security reports. Please review and sign so we can exchange the full pen test PDF.

DocuSign envelope: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123-secure

On the vulnerability SLA: Redwood's default public disclosure/remediation path is: 
- Critical/high: 30 days to remediation or documented mitigation; immediate notification and a 48-hour hotline during initial remediation.
- Medium: 60 days.
- Low: 90 days and best-effort patch scheduling.

We can agree to 45 days for criticals for MedAlpha on a case-by-case basis if you have contractual constraints; if you prefer 45 days, we'll add an exception for DEAL-9821 in the mutual action plan. Please confirm which SLA you prefer and who at MedAlpha will be the technical point-of-contact for vulnerability triage (name + email).

Thanks — I'll also upload the signed NDA and vendor questionnaire to a secure folder and share the link once complete.

—Aditya
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Priyanka Desai <pri@medalpha.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, MedAlpha Security Team <security@medalpha.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T16:30:00Z
Subject: Re: DocuSign: Redwood vendor-sharing NDA + questions on vulnerability SLA

Aditya — we signed the DocuSign envelope this morning. Our security lead for triage will be Sameer Patel (sameer.patel@medalpha.com). Regarding SLA, we can accept Redwood's default 30-day window for criticals only if both parties commit to an accelerated remediation workflow; otherwise we prefer 45 days. For this deal, let's add a 45-day exception in the mutual action plan and agree to review in the first 90 days post-go-live.

I'll ask Sameer to coordinate with Neha on technical handoff once you share the secure link to the full report.

Thanks,
Priyanka

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Desai <pri@medalpha.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T09:30:00Z
Subject: RE: Next steps: security artifacts, pen test report & vulnerability disclosure workflow

Great — thanks for the quick turnaround and for signing the NDA. Summary of agreed next steps so we have alignment:

1) Priyanka / MedAlpha: Full pen test report will be uploaded to the secure DocuSign/drive link for Sameer to share with Neha once privileges are granted.
2) SLA: Add a DEAL-9821 mutual action plan exception: 45 days for critical/high remediation (review at 90 days post-go-live).
3) Redwood: I will pre-fill the vendor questionnaire with Redwood-specific answers and upload to the shared secure folder. See attached placeholder (redwood_mutual_action_plan_link.txt).
4) Security techs: Neha and Sameer to schedule a 30-min triage call next week to review findings and proposed mitigation timelines.

If that matches your understanding, we’ll update the HubSpot deal and mark "security artifacts in progress." Appreciate the prompt cooperation — I’ll send the calendar invite for the triage call once the full report is available.

Best,
Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
